newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends off highs as supply still ample.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends off highs as supply still ample.

text.p: NYMEX crude ended off its highs Thursday as early gains made on a lower-than-expected April Brent loadings schedule were retraced on views domestic supply was ample.
"The Brent loading program assisted us here as the strength in London was carried over to the NYMEX," said Prudential Securities oil market analyst Richard Redash.
April crude settled up eight cents at $20.70 a barrel.
The North Sea Brent crude oil loading program for April has been set at 35 full cargoes plus 1.4 million barrels, making the program eight full cargoes less than March.

April crude had risen as much as 26 cents to $21.11 a barrel. Earlier this week, crude led the oil complex sharply lower on talk of a bevy of imports heading into the U.S. Gulf. The Brent schedule initially eased fears of North Sea exports.

"There is still plenty of supply, so there is a bearish tone to the market. I expect us to test $20.00 again" Redash said. The American Petroleum Institute said Wednesday that U.S. crude inventory grew 6.8 million barrels last week.
April heating oil ended up 0.14 cent at 54.22 cents a gallon while April gasoline settled off 0.40 cent at 64.23 cents a gallon.
A cold snap expected to hit the northeastern United States early next week buoyed heating oil prices.

Jon Davis, meteorologist with Smith Barney in Chicago, expects temperatures in the region to average seven to 11 degrees below normal from Sunday to Tuesday. The U.S. Northeast is the largest heating oil market in the world.
Heating oil was also boosted by short covering as a way to take profits from a gasoline-to-heat spread play.
"There was a lot of selling in the gasoline-to-heat spread," a New York gasoline trader said.
He explained that several weeks ago traders had bought gasoline and established short positions in heating oil expecting gasoline prices to rise and heating oil prices to fall, which they did.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
